label: Women graduates with moderate daily use and elevated loneliness
summary: This profile is characterized by comparatively higher loneliness alongside relatively low depressive and anxiety symptoms. It suggests respondents who feel more socially disconnected than other groups, without showing similarly elevated general mood or anxiety difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Female respondents, graduate education or above, and 1-3 hours of daily use.
behavior_markers: Shows relatively low depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean 0.86).
Shows relatively low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean 0.91).
Demographically anchored in women with higher education and moderate daily use.
tone: Socially disconnected but otherwise emotionally stable, with loneliness standing out more than depression or anxiety.

label: Profile 1: High loneliness, depression, and anxiety
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively elevated loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms across the measured indicators.
demographic_anchor: More likely to be female, have graduate-level education or above, and report more than 5 hours in the referenced time-use category.
behavior_markers: Higher average loneliness score on the UCLA-8 measure
Higher average depressive symptom score on the PHQ-9
Higher average anxiety symptom score on the GAD-7
Represents a training-split subgroup of 165 respondents

label: Low distress, socially connected profile
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and very low anxiety symptoms, indicating an overall low-distress mental health pattern.
demographic_anchor: Male respondents with graduate-level education or higher, commonly reporting 1-3 hours.
behavior_markers: Lower UCLA-8 loneliness scores than higher-distress profiles
Very low GAD-7 anxiety symptom levels
Overall pattern suggests relatively strong social connectedness and emotional stability
